# LingoFuse

> LingoFuse is a cross-language RPC framework — a communication foundation, not an AI agent framework. It enables functions written in any language to be called directly from any other language, without IDL, without stub generation, and without setting up HTTP services. Same-machine IPC latency is below 1 ms, with built-in service discovery, load balancing, FIFO ordering, and automatic reconnection. It is designed for any scenario where heterogeneous systems need to talk, and it happens to be an excellent substrate for AI agent toolchains.
>
> LingoFuse 是一个跨语言 RPC 框架，是通讯地基，不是智能体框架。任何语言写的函数，任何其他语言都能直接调——不写 IDL，不生成桩代码，不搭 HTTP 服务。同机 IPC 延迟低于 1 ms，内置服务发现、负载均衡、FIFO 顺序保证和断线重连。它适用于任何异构系统需要对话的场景，同时也是 AI 智能体工具链的优秀底座。

## Key facts

- Repository: https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse
- License: MIT
- Status: Active development (project started 2026)
- Core engine: C4 service mesh (Pascal core, pure C ABI)
- IPC latency: < 1 ms (self-reported, verify with `test/`)
- Built-in features: Service discovery, load balancing, FIFO ordering, automatic reconnection
- No IDL required, no stub generation required, no HTTP service required
- First-party bindings: Pascal, Python, C++, C#, TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, Go, Dart, Java, and PHP (caller-only via HTTP bridge)
- CI status: **C++ only** (GitHub-hosted; other languages have runnable local tests but no GitHub-hosted CI)
- Maintenance model: Single author; users are expected to be able to build and maintain the core library themselves if needed
- Related project: zIPC — https://github.com/PassByYou888/zIPC
- Code generator: LingoFuse-Tools — https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-Tools

## Stability first, concurrency secondary

LingoFuse places application **stability** as the top priority; concurrency performance is deliberately deprioritized. This is not a temporary trade-off but a trend the project will maintain in all future versions. A communication layer that occasionally crashes, drops messages, or deadlocks under high concurrency is useless no matter how low its latency is. Therefore, this project does not include horizontal performance comparisons in the main README. For actual measured data under concurrency and stress, refer to the `test/` directory.

## Core capabilities

- Cross-language function calls without IDL or stub generation
- Sub-1ms same-machine IPC latency (self-reported; verify locally)
- Built-in service discovery, load balancing, and FIFO ordering
- Streaming RPC support (Notify)
- Automatic reconnection
- Zero-copy data transfer
- HTTP bridge for browser / Node.js / PHP integration
- PHP integration via HTTP bridge (JSON over HTTP POST, PHP as caller only)
- Deterministic code generation via LingoFuse-Tools
- AI-ready knowledge base system for interface takeover

## Language support matrix

### First-party bindings (in-repo)

| Language | Status | Server | Client | Test scale | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Pascal** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | Full dev suite | Native FFI, core engine source |
| **Python** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | Full pipeline | `pip install -e .`, `@expose` decorator, HTTP bridge, JSON repair |
| **C++** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | **Only GitHub CI** | Native C ABI, zero overhead; functional / stress / concurrent test suites |
| **C# / .NET** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | **58 tests, 8 categories** | P/Invoke + RAII + unified JSON I/O |
| **TypeScript** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | **127 tests** | Complete type definitions; Node / Deno / Bun support |
| **JavaScript** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | **127 tests** | CommonJS + ESM dual entry; byte-level interop with TS |
| **Rust** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | **67 tests** | Safe RAII wrappers + full C ABI layer; `catch_unwind` at FFI boundary |
| **Go** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | **18 tests** | purego (no cgo), cross-compile friendly; e2e / ABI smoke / data handle tests |
| **Dart** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | Full test suite | Dart FFI + C bridge DLL; full caller + server capability; Flutter mobile support |
| **Java** | Production-ready | ✅ | ✅ | Automated tests | FFM API (JDK 22+), pure Java no JNI; `DataHandle` / `AppHandle`, three-process Demo; performance optimization ongoing |
| **PHP** | Caller-only | ❌ | ✅ | No FFI tests | Via `bridge.py` HTTP gateway, JSON over HTTP POST. **PHP cannot be a server.** Official PHP FFI cannot support C ABI callbacks. |

> **Java note**: Requires JDK 22+ (JDK 25 LTS recommended). Functionally complete, including cross-process RPC, cross-language ABI verification, and three-process Demo. Performance optimization is still in progress. GitHub-hosted CI currently covers C++ only; Java tests run locally via `java/run_test_ci.ps1` / `run_test_ci.sh`.

> **PHP note**: PHP can only act as a caller. If you need PHP as a server, LingoFuse currently does not satisfy that requirement.

### Via code generator / bridge

| Language / Platform | Method | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| **Node.js / Browser** | `bridge.py` HTTP gateway | Usable, non-native |
| **Kotlin / Swift / Ruby / Lua / Elixir / Julia / Zig / Nim / Crystal** | Via LingoFuse-Tools code generator | Generated code usable, requires own verification |
| **aarch64 / loongarch64 / RISC-V** | Edge device porting planned | In progress, not production-ready |

## Quick start

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse.git
cd LingoFuse
```

Then read the test guides under `test/` and run the pre-compiled executables inside `test.zip`. You get real data from your own hardware.

For deeper verification, compile the C++ CI tests yourself:

```bash
cd cpp/test   && cmake . && make && ./test_lingofuse
cd cpp/Stress && cmake . && make && ./StressService & ./StressClient
cd cpp/Conc   && cmake . && make && ./ConcService  & ./ConcClient
```

## Building the dynamic library

`src/` is the entry point for building the LingoFuse core dynamic library. Prepare a Pascal compilation environment (FPC / Lazarus), then one-click build.

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [`src/CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/src/CONTRIBUTING.md) | Build environment setup and workflow |
| [`src/CONTRIBUTING_lazbuild.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/src/CONTRIBUTING_lazbuild.md) | One-click build with lazbuild CLI |
| [`src/FPC_3.3.1_Package_Info.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/src/FPC_3.3.1_Package_Info.md) | FPC 3.3.1 environment package info |
| [`src/Lazarus_Change_FPC.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/src/Lazarus_Change_FPC.md) | Switching FPC version in Lazarus |

## Testing & verification: `test/` is the source of truth

For any uncertainty about the README — latency, ordering, stability, behavior under concurrency — **do not guess. Go to `test/` and find physical verification.**

### What `test/` provides

`test/` provides part of the **PoC (Proof of Concept)** work. Before using LingoFuse in production, note:

1. **The author provides race-condition stability tests (the most important mechanism-level tests), but not your App-level tests.** You need to simulate your own App layer and run a PoC to verify LF's behavior in your specific business scenario.
2. **You need to be able to build and compile LF yourself.** LingoFuse is developed by Lao Zhang; if it is not maintained long-term, users need to build it themselves and keep up with generational updates.
3. **Each language has its own test / CI system in principle.** Currently Pascal, C#, C++, JS, TS, Python, Rust, Go, Dart, and Java all have runnable tests, but **GitHub-hosted CI is C++ only**. Other languages provide local test scripts or projects:
   - C++: `cpp/test/`, `cpp/Stress/`, `cpp/Conc/`
   - Java: `java/run_test_ci.ps1`, `java/run_test_ci.sh`
   - Go: `go/test.ps1`, `go/dev_test.ps1`
   - Rust: `rust/test.ps1`
   - C#: `csharp/build.ps1`, `csharp/test/`
   - TypeScript: `ts/package.json`, `ts/test/`
   - Python: `Py/lingofuse/test_lingofuse.py`, `Py/lingofuse/test_bridge.py`
   - JavaScript: `js/test/test.js`
   - Dart: `dart/test/`
   - Pascal: various Demo and test projects under `pascal/`

### Why `test/` contains documents and executables instead of GitHub Actions

GitHub's automated CI has many limitations. LingoFuse supports **multiple languages and platforms** — Pascal, Python, C++, C#, TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, Go, Dart, Java, PHP, across Windows / Linux / macOS, covering IPC / TCP / cross-machine deployment forms. Putting all combinations into GitHub's hosted runners is neither convenient nor realistic.

So LingoFuse's approach is: **deliver testing capability directly to the user.** `test/` provides complete test guides (Markdown) and pre-compiled executables (`test.zip`). You extract, run, and observe on your own machine — getting **real data from your own hardware**.

**All GitHub-hosted CI tests are C++ code.** Source code can be found under `cpp/`:

- `cpp/test/` — Functional tests (`test_lingofuse.cpp` / `test_lingofuse_json.cpp`)
- `cpp/Stress/` — Stress tests (`StressService.cpp` / `StressClient.cpp` / `StressMonitor.cpp`)
- `cpp/Conc/` — Concurrent Notify tests (`ConcService.cpp` / `ConcClient.cpp`)

Each subdirectory has `CMakeLists.txt` and one-click CI scripts.

### Test documents & executables

| Document | Content | Executables |
|---|---|---|
| [`LingoFuse_Functional_Test_Guide.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/test/LingoFuse_Functional_Test_Guide.md) | **Functional tests**: 82 tests covering C++ RAII layer and serialization layer, verifying every public API contract. 100% pass in CI mode. | `test.zip` contains `test_lingofuse` / `test_lingofuse_json` |
| [`LingoFuse_Stress_Test_Guide.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/test/LingoFuse_Stress_Test_Guide.md) | **Stress tests**: One-click self-evaluation for Call / Notify / mixed modes, producing throughput, latency, and stability data on your own machine. | `test.zip` contains `StressService` / `StressClient` / `StressMonitor` |
| [`LingoFuse_Concurrent_Notify_Demo.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/test/LingoFuse_Concurrent_Notify_Demo.md) | **Concurrent Notify**: Verifies Notify is lossless under high concurrency, demonstrates the "completion barrier" pattern, 20 batches × 10,000 messages with zero loss. | `test.zip` contains `ConcService` / `ConcClient` |

### Language-specific test suites

#### Rust test suite

The Rust binding ships with **67 tests** across four layers, all passing:

| Layer | Command | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unit tests | `cargo test --lib` | 54 passed, 11 ignored (parallel-safe) |
| Ignored unit tests | `cargo test --lib -- --ignored --test-threads=1` | 11 passed (mutates process-global native state) |
| ABI smoke tests | `cargo test --test abi_smoke` | 5 passed (raw C ABI layer) |
| End-to-end integration | `cargo test --test framework_e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1` | 2 passed (full call + notify flow) |

See [`rust/README.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/rust/README.md) for full usage instructions.

#### Go test suite

The Go binding ships with tests under `go/test/`:

| Test file | Description |
|---|---|
| `abi_smoke_test.go` | ABI smoke test |
| `data_handle_test.go` | Data handle test |
| `e2e_test.go` | End-to-end test |
| `errors_test.go` | Error handling test |

Run with `go test ./...` from the `go/` directory. See [`go/README.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/go/README.md) for details.

#### C# test suite

The C# binding ships with **58 tests across 8 categories**: `DataHandle` (19), `AppHandle` (10), `LfIo` (7), `Framework` (5), network integration (8), cross-language ABI (5), concurrency (2), stress (2). See [`csharp/`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/tree/main/csharp) for details.

#### TypeScript / JavaScript test suite

The JS binding ships with **127 tests** (127 passed, 0 failed), covering native library loading, app creation, API registration, self-connected service + client startup, and end-to-end calls. See [`ts/`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/tree/main/ts) and [`js/`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/tree/main/js) for details.

#### Java test suite

The Java binding includes automated tests under `java/src/test/`. Run locally via:

```powershell
cd java
```

See [`java/README.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/java/README.md) for details.

#### Dart test suite

| Test file | Description |
|---|---|

See [`dart/README.md`](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse/blob/main/dart/README.md) for details.

## Code generator system

LingoFuse-Tools solves the biggest pain point of cross-language RPC: writing bindings for each language by hand.

Give it a Pascal unit or C header file, and it automatically produces multi-language server, client, and companion README documentation.

| Tool | Target | Protocol | Target languages |
|---|---|---|---|
| **code_decl_to_abi** | ABI server / client | LingoFuse binary ABI | Pascal / Python / C++ / C# / Rust / Go |
| **code_decl_to_json_abi** | HTTP/JSON server / client | HTTP + JSON (via bridge) | Pascal / Python / C++ / C# / JavaScript / PHP |
| **code_decl_to_mcp** | MCP tool provider | Model Context Protocol | Pascal / Python / C++ / C# |

Each tool has three entry points: GUI, CLI, and MCP API. Each tool comes with a self-contained knowledge base (Markdown) covering API contracts, wire protocol, type mapping, known pitfalls, debugging trees, and extension guides.

Feed the knowledge base to an AI, and the AI can assist in taking over the interface — generated code still requires human verification. The knowledge base and MCP API are generated from the same source, so they never diverge.

See: https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-Tools

## Ecosystem projects built on LingoFuse

LingoFuse is a communication foundation. The foundation itself does not build applications, but many kinds of buildings can be built on top of it.

### Agent runtimes

| Project | Language | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [pasAgent v2](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-pasAgent) | Pascal | Released | Text agent, 129+ LLM backends |
| [pasAgent v3](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-pasAgent-v3) | Pascal | Released | Multimodal agent, 250+ backends, dual-language code generation |
| [cppAgent](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-cppAgent) | C++ | Released | C++ ecosystem agent integration |
| [csharpAgent](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-csharpAgent) | C# / .NET | Released | .NET agent runtime + LLM client SDK |
| **tsAgent** | TypeScript | Coming soon | TypeScript / JavaScript ecosystem agent runtime |

> **tsAgent is not yet released.** The current TS/JS bindings are pure communication layers, without an agent runtime. If you need to build agents in TS/JS, use mature frameworks like Mastra or Vercel AI SDK, then call functions in other languages through LingoFuse's TS bindings.

These branches demonstrate that the LingoFuse communication foundation is general enough to support agent layers built in any language ecosystem — and the foundation ensures they can talk to each other.

### Related projects

- **[zIPC](https://github.com/PassByYou888/zIPC)** — The same-machine IPC engine under LingoFuse. Use zIPC directly if you only need same-machine IPC without the full RPC mesh.
- **[ZNetV2](https://github.com/PassByYou888/ZNetV2)** — The large-scale server-side data throughput framework in the PassByYou888 stack.

## Dependencies

Core dynamic libraries are located in `Binary/`:

| Platform | Core library | IPC dependency | Memory allocator |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows 64 | `LingoFuse64.dll` | `z_ipc_64.dll` | `mimalloc64.dll` |
| Windows 32 | `LingoFuse32.dll` | `z_ipc_32.dll` | `mimalloc32.dll` |
| Linux | `liblingofuse.so` | `libz_ipc.so` | `libmimalloc.so` (optional) |
| macOS | `liblingofuse.dylib` | `libz_ipc.dylib` | `libmimalloc.dylib` (optional) |

> The current `Binary/` directory mainly provides Windows 32/64-bit pre-compiled libraries. Linux / macOS libraries must be compiled according to the build documents under `src/`.

**Deployment**: Add the `Binary/` directory to system `PATH`, or copy the dynamic libraries to the executable's directory.

On Windows, install the **VC++ 2015-2022 Redistributable**:
- Download page: [Latest supported Visual C++ Redistributable downloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170)
- x64 direct link: [vc_redist.x64.exe](https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe)
- x86 direct link: [vc_redist.x86.exe](https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x86.exe)

## Not recommended for

- Projects requiring mature community support, extensive third-party tutorials, or Stack Overflow Q&A.
- Teams that cannot accept single-maintainer risk and lack the ability to compile and maintain LF themselves.
- Pure TS/JS projects where all logic can be rewritten in TS/JS — introducing LF only adds complexity and failure points.
- Scenarios requiring PHP as a server (PHP can only be a caller).
- Teams with hard concurrency performance requirements who are unwilling to run their own App-level PoC verification.
- **Flutter Web projects** (Dart FFI unavailable).
- **32-bit Windows projects** (Dart binding untested).
- **Java binding requires JDK 22+**; cannot run directly on JDK 8 / 11 / 17 / 21.
